text:
Franklin County ranks 12th in Maine for project-based Section 8 assisted units in 2025
N. J. Cohen
Franklin County ranked 12th of 16 Maine counties in the project-based Section 8 assisted-unit ranking for 2025, with 159 assisted units reported.
The county's assisted-unit total remained at 159, unchanged from 2024.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally lower rents for low-income households that meet program eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households outlines three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households that receive HUD rental assistance typically pay 30% of their income after deductions, with the federal government covering the remainder. Eligibility depends on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are generally placed on waiting lists until assistance is available.
